name: xswl
blurb: Chinese abbreviation of 笑死我了, "I'm dying of laughter", like LMAO
title: XSWL Meaning: What Does XSWL Mean in Chinese?
description: XSWL is short for 笑死我了 (xiào sǐ wǒ le), "I'm dying of laughter", the Chinese LMAO. How to use it, with examples and similar terms.
answer: XSWL is the pinyin initialism of 笑死我了 (xiào sǐ wǒ le), "it's killing me, I'm dying of laughter". It means something is hilarious, much like LMAO. It belongs to a family of pinyin abbreviations popular with young Chinese users; China Youth Daily used it as a textbook example when it reported on teenagers' online slang in 2018.

body: Pinyin initialisms take the first letter of each syllable of a common phrase. They are faster to type and feel like an in-group code. 笑死我了 was already an everyday exaggeration for "so funny", and its initials became a fixture of comments and bullet chats.

In October 2018 China Youth Daily quoted the line "你连 dbq 都不知道，xswl！" ("You don't even know dbq? XSWL!") to show how teenagers talk online. There is no record of where the abbreviation first appeared.

ul: xswl，猫把自己卡在纸箱里了 (LMAO, the cat got stuck in a box)
xswl，你这刘海是认真的吗 (LMAO, were those bangs a choice?)

body: XSWL is light and friendly between friends. Replying XSWL to someone's bad news or a serious post reads as mocking them.
People unfamiliar with internet slang may not recognise it, so in formal messages just write 太好笑了 ("so funny").

faq.a: 笑死我了, xiào sǐ wǒ le: "laughing me to death", or "I'm dying of laughter".
No. It just means something is funny, but using it about someone's embarrassment can come across as laughing at them.

faq.q: What is the English equivalent of XSWL?
faq.a: LMAO or "I'm dead". It is a bit stronger than LOL.
